name: KC-135 Stratotanker
summary: Four-engine aerial refueling tanker based on the Boeing 367-80/707 design; still the most numerous USAF tanker, flown heavily by Guard and Reserve units.

wings: Low-mounted swept wing with noticeable dihedral
Plain wingtips with no winglets; some aircraft carry hose-drogue pods at the outer wing
engines: Four large high-bypass turbofans in fat nacelles on individual pylons
fuselage: Narrow single-deck fuselage, shorter than a 707 airliner
Flying refueling boom hanging beneath the tail, with a boom operator's window under the rear fuselage
tail: Tall swept single vertical fin with a thin antenna probe at the top

tellTales: Refueling boom hanging under the tail of a four-engine jet
Almost no cabin windows along a narrow fuselage
Four fat high-bypass engines on pylons under a swept low wing

confusedWith.howToTell: The KC-135 has four engines and a narrow fuselage; the KC-46 has two big engines on a wider widebody fuselage.
The KC-135 has a refueling boom and a plain nose and sides; the RC-135 has a long thimble nose, cheek fairings and many belly antennas but no boom.
The KC-135 has a boom and plain wingtips on a shorter fuselage; the E-6 has wingtip pods, no boom and a longer fuselage.
The KC-135 has no radar disc and has high-bypass engines; the E-3 carries a large rotating radar disc on struts above the rear fuselage.

usCount.source: USAF KC-135 fact sheet / FlightGlobal World Air Forces 2026
